question.text: A PMS client accumulating wealth should REBALANCE via:

answer.text: Prioritise inflow allocation to underweight buckets (tax-efficient)

explanation.text: The Logic: During accumulation, an investor still has fresh inflows (salary, savings, bonuses) entering the portfolio. Directing those inflows toward asset buckets that are currently underweight nudges allocations back to target without selling overweight holdings. Avoiding sales avoids realising capital gains, which keeps the rebalance tax-efficient and lets the existing positions continue to compound. The Trap: "Only selling overweight" forces unnecessary gain realisation and tax outflow during a phase when the investor still has new cash to deploy. "Not rebalance" abandons risk control and lets drift accumulate. "Withdraw" is the opposite of accumulation behaviour. Note: This specific accumulation-phase, inflow-directed rebalancing recommendation is not explicitly stated in the cited NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook pages (311, 385, 396-397); the workbook discusses tax cost on selling appreciated assets, but not inflow-allocation as a tactic. The framing above reflects general portfolio-management practice for tax-efficient rebalancing.
